hook.line: At the neighbourhood meeting you want to say you are on board. But backing a plan and agreeing with a person are two different phrases in Spanish.
hook.en: I'm in favour of the plan.

examples.en: I'm in favour of the plan.

examples.es: No estoy de acuerdo con Vale.
Mariana está de acuerdo con Tomás.
Don Hernando está a favor de la idea.
examples.en: Don Hernando is in favour of the idea.

rule:
Both phrases mean "I'm on board", but they answer different questions.

*Estar a favor de*: you take a side on a thing, such as a plan, an idea or doing something. *Estoy a favor del plan.*

*Estar de acuerdo con*: you agree with a person or with what they said. *Estoy de acuerdo con Vale.*

The opposites are *estar en contra de* and *no estar de acuerdo con*. Both use *estar*, never *ser*, and each keeps its own little word: *a favor de*, *de acuerdo con*.
smallPrint: Teachers call both of these stance phrases: one marks support for a proposal, the other agreement with a speaker.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *a favor* or *de acuerdo* and type the whole sentence: *Estoy ___ del plan.*
yourTurn.why: A plan is a thing you back, so *a favor de* (*de* + *el* is *del*).

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *a favor* or *de acuerdo* and type the whole sentence: *Estoy ___ con Vale.*
yourTurn.why: You agree with a person, so *de acuerdo con*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Mariana agrees with Tomás.
yourTurn.answer: Mariana está de acuerdo con Tomás.
yourTurn.why: A person again, so *está de acuerdo con*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I'm in favour of selling.
yourTurn.why: After *a favor de*, an infinitive works: *vender*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: Do you agree?
yourTurn.why: To a friend, *estás*; agreeing is a position you are in.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Estoy de acuerdo con Vale.* Say: I don't agree with Vale.
yourTurn.answer: No estoy de acuerdo con Vale.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Don Hernando is in favour of the idea.
yourTurn.answer: Don Hernando está a favor de la idea.
yourTurn.why: An idea is a thing to back, so *a favor de*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Agreeing is a position you are in, so Spanish uses *estar*.
Almost. To agree with a person, use *de acuerdo con*; *a favor* takes *de* and backs a thing.
Almost. It is always *con* after *de acuerdo*.

personal: Think of something a friend said lately and a plan in your town. Say *Estoy de acuerdo con...* for one and *Estoy a favor de...* for the other.
